prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and bioactive form of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based therapy of diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B010 as a single achievement for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case rests on the chain of evidence, not on the six matching first places. Holst established in humans how GLP-1 is secreted and what it does, Mojsov identified the bioactive truncated peptide, and Drucker worked out receptor biology and showed the peptide could be exploited therapeutically. Independent randomized trials of the resulting agonists in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease have confirmed the clinical result, so the interpretation is stable and the timing is not in question. The prize would reward discovery of a mechanism and its human benefit. A pairing with a second part would add nothing to this case and would force a split of three names across two achievements, with less secure credit on the second.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point and round 1 did not remove it. Mojsov's priority over the Habener group for the bioactive peptide is unverified by any of us, Habener is not a credited name on the ballot, and the three-name cap leaves out Knudsen, whose half-life-extension chemistry is a real scientific contribution. A prize built on this allocation could age worse than a cleaner pairing. If the priority question were settled against Mojsov, the supplied ballot gives no replacement name and the configuration would need to be revisited.

responses.point: The chair says the committee may be settling the B010 allocation too quickly because the support is so uniform, and that the configuration fails if the three names cannot be defended on documented priority.
responses.response: I agree and take this as the main condition on my position. My round-1 statement relied on recall for the Mojsov and Habener question. I have not read the primary papers and cannot do so within this stage, so I will not claim that I resolved it. What I can say is that the discovery stands whichever way the dispute falls: the physiology, the receptor biology and the outcome trials are not in doubt, and only one of the three names is at risk. My position therefore stays, but it is conditional. If a documentary check showed Mojsov's contribution to be derivative of the Habener group's, I would withdraw support for this trio and ask for a name set the supplied ballot does not offer, instead of substituting Knudsen by default.

responses.point: Perlmann would not reduce B006 to June and Sadelain until the Eshhar question is resolved, and he ranks B020 as a clean alternative while noting that PERK and ATF6 lie outside the Walter and Mori core.
responses.response: I accept the point on B006: the Eshhar gap applies to every version, so I have changed the order of my alternatives and put B020 first and B006 second. Walter and Mori cover the Ire1 and HAC1/XBP1 core with the clearest priority on the list. Your PERK and ATF6 caveat is a fair limit on the citation, which should be worded around the Ire1 branch and not the whole response. It also leaves B020 with mainly conceptual medical relevance, which is why I keep it as an alternative and not as a rival to B010.

responses.point: El-Manira treats B008 (optogenetics) as a legitimate alternative because the Prize has rewarded methods that opened intractable questions, and words his citation around establishing the incretin axis.
responses.response: I agree that the Prize has rewarded methods, and I would not exclude optogenetics on that principle alone. My objection to B008 is the credit structure: six names, a split between discovery and deployment, and no documented basis in the supplied record for ranking Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann ahead of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck. I also see little clinical reach so far, which matters for a Physiology or Medicine prize. On your citation wording, I prefer the form that says the discoveries made the therapies possible. That recognizes the physiology as the enabling step without implying that the committee is naming the drugs, and it does not suggest that Knudsen's work was incidental.

responses.point: Linnarsson would treat Knudsen as first reserve rather than displace a discoverer, and he ranked B045 (SMN2 antisense) third in the opening round.
responses.response: I agree that Knudsen is the first reserve for B010 if one of the three names weakens, and that the cap, not a view of her work, explains her exclusion. I would not move her ahead of Drucker or Holst, because the physiology is the discovery the citation rewards. If it were Mojsov who weakened, Knudsen would not be a like-for-like replacement, since she would be filling a discovery seat with a development contribution. That is a reason to settle the priority question first. On B045 I still see a clear mechanism-to-drug arc, but it is younger and risks being read as recognition of antisense technology in general, so I do not put it among my two alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the bioactive GLP-1(7-36) peptide can be separated from the Habener group's work. This is based on recall and has not been checked against primary papers.
Whether the committee will accept a three-name B010 if that check is inconclusive, given that the ballot offers no replacement for Mojsov other than Knudsen.

Whether the citation should name only the physiology and bioactive peptide or also state that it made the drugs possible. I favour the latter wording but am uncertain how it will be read against Knudsen's exclusion.
If B010 does not reach four votes, the fallback remains unclear. B020 has the cleanest credit but modest medical impact, and B006 has a fragile attribution without Eshhar.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and share an institution (Karolinska Institutet) with colleagues. None of the shortlisted candidates or credited names is connected to my work or collaborators, and I see no basis for recusal on any ballot.
